data.title: Demand Gen Replaced Video Action Campaigns: Everything You Need to Know Now
data.excerpt: Demand Gen replaced Google's Video Action Campaigns. What changed, the new features worth using and the migration mistakes to check in your account.

children.text: According to Google Ads Help

, Google stopped allowing new Video Action Campaigns (VAC) in April 2025, began upgrading existing ones to Demand Gen automatically in July 2025 and set April 2026 as the deadline for the last ones. In 2026, some advertisers still don’t fully understand the new format — some because they migrated without reviewing settings, others because they entered Demand Gen directly without context of what it replaces. This is the guide you need.
What Is Demand Gen and How Does It Differ from VAC?

Video Action Campaigns were YouTube campaigns focused on generating direct conversions — landing page clicks, app installs, purchases. Demand Gen maintains that objective but expands inventory and capabilities:
Expanded inventory:
includes YouTube (Shorts, In-Stream, In-Feed), Discover, Gmail and the Google Display Network — not just YouTube like VACs.
Visual formats:
can use images in addition to video — more like intelligent Display than a pure video campaign.
AI creative:
Demand Gen can generate video variations using AI, directly from the platform.
Improved audience signals:
deeper integration with Google Audiences and Customer Match.
New Features That Change Strategy
Three features Google added to Demand Gen in 2025, according to its
year-end highlights
Target CPC bidding:
allows setting a target CPC — something VACs didn’t have. Useful for advertisers who need click cost control in quality traffic campaigns.
New customer acquisition goal:
according to Google, it optimizes the campaign to attract new or high-value customers. Useful if you have up-to-date CRM lists.
Auto-generated videos:
if you don’t have your own video, Google can generate videos with AI to extend your reach on YouTube. Reduces the entry barrier for e-commerce with large catalogs.
If you sell products, also see
Google Lens and Shopping Ads
The Most Common Migration Errors
The most reported problems in accounts that migrated from VAC to Demand Gen without review:
Poorly configured audiences:
automatic migration doesn’t always correctly transfer audience signals — verify manually.
Insufficient budget for expanded inventory:
Demand Gen covers more channels, needs more budget to learn correctly.
Video-only creative:
not leveraging available images in Demand Gen reduces accessible inventory.
How to Get the Most from Demand Gen in 2026

The optimal configuration combines: Customer Match-based audience signals, mixed creative (video + image), conversion objective with sufficient historical data, and the new customer acquisition goal if remarketing is managed in separate campaigns.
Conclusion

Demand Gen isn’t an inferior replacement for VACs — it’s a more capable format with more complexity. Advertisers who understand its differences and configure correctly are seeing results superior to their previous video campaigns. Those who migrated on autopilot are not.

Performance Max vs Search

children.text: Were my VAC campaigns automatically migrated to Demand Gen?

Yes, if you didn't upgrade them yourself. According to Google Ads Help, Google began upgrading them automatically in July 2025 and set April 2026 as the deadline for the last ones. Automatic upgrades use some default settings and certain features don't carry over, so review each migrated campaign.
Is Demand Gen more expensive than VAC?
Not necessarily. Demand Gen covers more inventory, which may require more budget for the learning phase, but Target CPC and improved audiences can result in a lower CPA than original VACs.
Can I use only video in Demand Gen?
You can, but you shouldn't. Demand Gen supports images in addition to video, and using both formats significantly expands available inventory and improves campaign performance.
